statement.smallest_supported_claim: After the declared native save/reload process replacement, the same run exposed Bugchaser central and its accessible storage, and Katharina Leach (character:2) retained the saved camp assignment, follower rule, priority, identity, and 17-item inventory. A later native pause was accepted and advanced the game turn, showing ordinary behavior resumed.
statement.causal_account: The post-reload observation is bound to run d7929b2e62413e227fde942eebe5e00bcab02f9c5bc8639c48b41be41ae8bdd8 and binding 3a5dbb5f23ae3a7334e22ae8233e67a96453fb9c29a72fd6cbc682ba86505dd2. Native NPC inspection reports the same actor identity and durable values after reload; the storage snapshot retains all seven pre-save entries. Native world.pause receipts are accepted on the relaunched owner, and the follow-up inspection retains the same values.

citations.meaning: Exact source, executable, scenario, run, and binding identity for the sealed witness.
Fresh post-reload World owner exposes the saved camp and accessible storage.
Post-reload native NPC inspection exposes Katharina's exact identity, assignment, rule, priority, and inventory count.
The first ordinary native pause after reload was accepted on the relaunched owner.
The resumed world returned to native NPC inspection at the next game turn.
After the control and a later native pause, the camp/storage state remains present and unchanged at the cited item boundary.
A second ordinary native pause was accepted after the free-text control.

remaining_unknowns: The compact journal does not itself carry the child process-instance field; the bridge manifest and stale-frame rejection artifact provide the lifecycle/process-generation evidence.
No movement/separation claim was made; resumed behavior here is limited to accepted ordinary turns and stable state inspection.

statement.smallest_supported_claim: The independently receipted unaddressed free-text utterance was accepted, but after one native turn the world displayed a second Katharina camp-craft response as well as the ordinary follower response; therefore this run does not establish the declared control property that the unaddressed control does not queue the addressed camp-craft route.
statement.causal_account: The native chat/menu/prompt chain was accepted with exact frame-bound receipts. The later World observation records the submitted utterance, a new Katharina craft response, and a subsequent R031 Route Ally 1 response. The storage item boundary remains unchanged, so no duplicate item mutation was observed, but the routing-control expectation itself was not met.

citations.meaning: The unaddressed free-text prompt submission was accepted by the native owner.
The post-control native messages include the second Katharina craft response and the ordinary follower response.

checks.value.surface.facts.messages.239.text: Katharina Leach says, "Heard you.  1 × bandages matched bandage, but it's blocked: Camp storage could not supply the needed ingredients or tools."
checks.value.surface.facts.messages.240.text: R031 Route Ally 1 says: "Sure thing, Zoraida—hand-crafting bandages now for you."

material_deviations: The expected unaddressed-control non-queue property was not demonstrated; a camp response was observed.
The same craft utterance was used as the control, so the response is evidence of observed routing, not proof of a distinct addressed request identity.
remaining_unknowns: The retained native surface does not expose a structured camp-request ID for the second free-text utterance.

findings.observed_defect: The post-reload free-text control produced a second Katharina camp-craft response instead of cleanly remaining outside the addressed camp-craft route.
findings.next_action: Trace the native free-text recipient/routing path and add a new-source witness that distinguishes an unaddressed utterance from the saved addressed craft request without recreating the addressed request.
